en.title: Scott Colom wins Mississippi Senate seat as Alaska race remains uncalled
en.dek: Democrat Scott Colom won the Mississippi Senate race, while ballot counting continues in Alaska and a new poll measures early interest in potential 2028 presidential contenders.
facts: Scott Colom defeated incumbent Republican Cindy Hyde-Smith in the Mississippi U.S. Senate election.
Colom is the first Black senator elected from Mississippi since the 19th century.
Former Representative Mary Peltola holds a narrow lead over Senator Dan Sullivan in the uncalled Alaska Senate race.
A court rejected a legal challenge from the Peltola campaign regarding rejected absentee ballots.
A new poll shows Republicans JD Vance and Marco Rubio leading early preferences for their party's 2028 nomination.
body: Democrat Scott Colom won the U.S. Senate election in Mississippi on 12 November, according to NPR and CNBC. He defeated the incumbent Republican senator, Cindy Hyde-Smith.

NPR and CNBC reported that Colom is the first Black senator elected to represent Mississippi since the 19th century. His victory changes the party representation for one of the state's two Senate seats.

Ballot counting remains underway in Alaska for the U.S. Senate race between former Representative Mary Peltola and Senator Dan Sullivan. The Hill and Fox News reported on 12 November that the race is still uncalled.

Peltola maintains a narrow lead in the total vote count, according to reporting from The Hill and Fox News. Sullivan narrowed that gap following recent vote tallies released by state election officials.

Legal action surrounding the Alaska contest reached a decision when a court ruled against the Peltola campaign regarding rejected absentee ballots. Fox News reported that the court denied the campaign's request to include those specific rejected ballots in the final tally.

Looking ahead to future elections, a new poll reported by The Jerusalem Post and The Hill shows Vice President JD Vance and Senator Marco Rubio favored for the 2028 Republican presidential nomination. Neither Vance nor Rubio has formally launched a campaign, and the nominating contests remain more than a year away.
en.context: The 2026 midterm elections determine the composition of the U.S. Senate. Formal nominating contests for the 2028 presidential election cycle begin in more than a year.

en.dek: Democrat Scott Colom defeated incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith in Mississippi, while the Alaska Senate race between Mary Peltola and Dan Sullivan continues.
body: Democrat Scott Colom won the U.S. Senate election in Mississippi on 12 November. According to NPR and CNBC, he defeated the incumbent Republican, Cindy Hyde-Smith.
Colom is the first Black senator elected from Mississippi since the 19th century, as reported by NPR and CNBC. This result marks a change in the state's Senate representation.

Alaska election officials continue to count ballots in the race between former Representative Mary Peltola and Senator Dan Sullivan. The Hill and Fox News reported that the race remains uncalled as of 12 November.
Peltola maintains a narrow lead in the vote count, according to The Hill and Fox News. Sullivan has gained ground following recent vote drops in the state.
The Peltola campaign recently lost a court case regarding rejected absentee ballots. Fox News stated that the court ruled against the campaign's attempt to include those ballots in the final tally.
Election officials in Alaska are processing the remaining ballots to determine the winner. Both The Hill and Fox News noted that the outcome depends on the final count.

de.dek: Der Demokrat Scott Colom besiegte die Amtsinhaberin Cindy Hyde-Smith in Mississippi, während das Senatsrennen in Alaska zwischen Mary Peltola und Dan Sullivan andauert.
body: Der Demokrat Scott Colom gewann am 12. November die US-Senatswahl in Mississippi. Laut NPR und CNBC besiegte er die republikanische Amtsinhaberin Cindy Hyde-Smith.

Colom ist der erste schwarze Senator, der seit dem 19. Jahrhundert in Mississippi gewählt wurde, wie NPR und CNBC berichteten. Dieses Ergebnis markiert einen Wechsel in der Senatsvertretung des Bundesstaates.

Wahlbeamte in Alaska zählen weiterhin die Stimmzettel im Rennen zwischen der ehemaligen Abgeordneten Mary Peltola und Senator Dan Sullivan. The Hill und Fox News berichteten, dass das Rennen zum 12. November noch nicht entschieden ist.
Peltola hält laut The Hill und Fox News einen knappen Vorsprung bei der Stimmenauszählung. Sullivan konnte nach jüngsten Stimmenzuwächsen im Bundesstaat Boden gutmachen.

Das Peltola-Wahlkampfteam verlor kürzlich einen Gerichtsprozess bezüglich abgelehnter Briefwahlunterlagen. Fox News gab an, dass das Gericht den Versuch des Wahlkampfteams, diese Stimmzettel in die endgültige Auszählung einzubeziehen, zurückwies.
Wahlbeamte in Alaska verarbeiten die verbleibenden Stimmzettel, um den Sieger zu ermitteln. Sowohl The Hill als auch Fox News merkten an, dass das Ergebnis von der endgültigen Auszählung abhängt.
facts: Scott Colom besiegte die republikanische Amtsinhaberin Cindy Hyde-Smith bei der US-Senatswahl in Mississippi.
Colom ist der erste schwarze Senator, der seit dem 19. Jahrhundert in Mississippi gewählt wurde.
Das Senatsrennen in Alaska zwischen Mary Peltola und Dan Sullivan ist weiterhin unentschieden.
Peltola führt in Alaska knapp, während die Auszählung der Stimmzettel andauert.
Ein Gericht wies eine Klage des Peltola-Wahlkampfteams bezüglich der Briefwahlunterlagen ab.
de.title: Scott Colom gewinnt Senatssitz in Mississippi, während Rennen in Alaska noch nicht entschieden ist
de.context: Die Zwischenwahlen 2026 bestimmen die Zusammensetzung des US-Senats. Diese Rennen sind Teil des umfassenderen nationalen Wahlzyklus.
